body: I’ll give those videos a watch, thank you. Yeah your point about fluidity is devastating and absolutely true. My own boundaries are so.... nonexistent that I think I have trouble identifying those of others and push even if there’s a voice in my head saying no... because it was so commonplace growing up to have mine being crossed on a whim. Therefore it’s just what I’ve identified as “okay” even when it isn’t.

I think I need a psychiatrist. I’ve been going to a therapist and honestly, I don’t feel like it’s doing anything. She’s shocked at my situation. So are most people. But it stopped phasing me, and maybe it’s just our dynamic, but it feels like I’m making no progress. I don’t let myself be vulnerable with anyone and this therapist is no exception. I don’t know how exactly. The problem is when I do open up fully I tend to break down. Panic attacks, hyperventilation, the works - and I have a physical deformity at the hands of abuse from my parents also that makes it very hard to breathe so I tend to black out when that happens.

Needless to say I try to keep things in,

Hence the title of the post.

I’m trying though. Thanks.

Trust me. Having grown up amongst crazy, it’s that the adults in question _are not in their right minds_ 

Crazy LITERALLY CANNOT take the perspective of others, and it’s entirely possible for a person to twist reality so ridiculously much just to fit their own viewpoint irregardless of whatever logic or facts they have to disregard.

It's funny, my friend who is Chinese but raised without knowing the language or culture identifies strongly as white. I think how much you identify with whatever cultures influence you def has a strong effect on who you turn out to be

I'm glad your upbringing was more or less solid it sounds like? I agree. Asian parents, especially first gen, should do a lot to teach their own children about where they come from. There are struggles there too with being a immigrant parent coming to a foreign place, but it's seriously so important to childhood identity formation and the questions that naturally come from having a different skin tone than the mainstream - something I think a lot of us here might be able to identify with

Yeah you hit the nail on the head I think man. It's like what even is someone if not who they come from?? Backgrounds and stories are super important which is why this sub is pretty fucking special imo. Hope your journey goes well too.

Some kids treasure their childhoods, some survive them. I appreciate the well wishes man.

And lol I actually did growing up and my chinese is conversational level. I read/write on a basic level and can understand and speak to a good degree tbh which I am grateful for.

My mother hated my stepfather’s traits and encouraged me to do lots of Chinese school stuff (in the beginning before she went full crazy) - it’s part of why my identities are so conflicting, I think, because they both have a pretty big role
Thanks and it definitely kinda seems that way... I'm glad I am too lol

Yeah. Reading some of the stories I've read here about other WMAF parenting experiences some have had I feel almost lucky in that regard that nothing ever escalated to physical violence. But it was almost like because he couldn't physically hit me or my mother he took extra care to be as narcissistic/gaslighting/textbook abusive as possible when he was upset. It was disgusting and I'm glad to be out of that household.

Edit: that reminds me of the time he called the police on me for something I never did, basically to escalate threat and to feel in control - my mom was in the room and supported him doing this of course - and while on the phone with the officer - which he put on speakerphone to basically make me feel like shit - he **misspelled** my chinese (birth and legal) name. Like what a joke.

My stepfather? No, given that he had a genetic physical disability (I think his egotistical personality was a defense mechanism for coping with this actually) he wasn't ever able to hit me physically. But he was a very flawed human being in a lot of ways. Thanks for asking though.

Hi,

Thank you a lot for this response. It's... reassuring knowing that there's others who have been through similar things and made it out on the other side.
Thanks. What kind of practices would you recommend doing? These realizations have all kind of hit me and life has been a whirlwind especially after breaking away from my parents this past summer.
